In [[algebraic geometry]], an '''ind-scheme''' is a set-valued [[functor]] that can be written (represented) as a [[direct limit]] (i.e., inductive limit) of [[closed immersion|closed embedding]] of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]].

== Examples ==
*<math>\mathbb{C}P^{\infty} = \varinjlim \mathbb{C}P^N</math> is an ind-scheme.
*Perhaps the most famous example of an ind-scheme is an [[infinite grassmannian]] (which is a quotient of the [[loop group]] of an [[algebraic group]] ''G''.)
